unitTitle.value: Autonomous Systems: Robotics and Computational Problem-Solving

description.value: Students work in collaborative teams to design, implement, and refine an autonomous robotic solution addressing a defined real-world challenge, utilizing agile project management tools to track development. The project requires students to document their design process through user stories and flowcharts, implement modular code in an object-oriented language, and conduct systematic debugging against established test cases. The final submission is a multimodal presentation evaluating the functional prototype against stakeholder requirements and the broader enterprising impact of autonomous systems.

conditions.value:
• Collaborative project team (3 students)
• Agile project management documentation (e.g., Kanban boards, sprint logs)
• Design portfolio (5–7 A3 pages or equivalent digital media) including user stories, flowcharts, pseudocode, and systematic testing/debugging records
• Functional robotic prototype demonstrating autonomous capability
• Multimodal presentation (maximum 5 minutes) evaluating the solution against design criteria, stakeholder requirements, and broader enterprising impact
• Supervised class time for iterative development and testing

resourcesAvailable.value:
Hardware: mBot sets, including expansion kits and supplementary sensors (ultrasonic, colour, force).
Project Management: Trello for agile sprint planning, task delegation, and tracking milestones.

context.value:
In this unit, students apply computational and design thinking to address complex, open-ended robotics challenges. By decomposing real-world scenarios, students define precise problem specifications and user stories to guide the iterative development of autonomous solutions. Students design, implement, and refine algorithms using object-oriented programming to control robotic hardware, employing flowcharts and pseudocode to verify the accuracy of their logic and ensure robust solution performance. Throughout the development process, students utilise systematic testing and debugging techniques to validate their solutions against specific design criteria.

Furthermore, students explore the interaction between hardware and software components, managing data flow and control structures within digital systems. By documenting their design process and evaluating the effectiveness of their robotic solutions, students reflect on the enterprising nature of their work and the broader impact of autonomous technologies. This unit fosters collaborative project management skills, requiring students to plan tasks, manage timelines, and evaluate their prototypes against stakeholder needs and functionality requirements.

task.value: Students work in collaborative teams to design, implement, and refine an autonomous robotic solution addressing a defined real-world challenge, utilizing agile project management tools to track development. The project requires students to document their design process through user stories and flowcharts, implement modular code in an object-oriented language, and conduct systematic debugging against established test cases. The final submission is a multimodal presentation evaluating the functional prototype against stakeholder requirements and the broader enterprising impact of autonomous systems.

toComplete.value:
To complete this task, you must work in collaborative teams to design, implement, and refine an autonomous robotic solution addressing a defined real-world challenge. You are required to:

*   **Define and decompose** the problem by interviewing stakeholders to establish precise design criteria and user stories.
*   **Utilise agile project management tools** (e.g., Kanban boards, sprint logs) to plan, track, and manage team responsibilities and timelines.
*   **Design algorithms** incorporating logical operators, representing them through formal flowcharts and pseudocode.
*   **Implement modular code** in an object-oriented programming language, applying selected algorithms and data structures to control the robotic hardware.
*   **Validate your solution** by conducting systematic testing and debugging, comparing output against established test cases to ensure robust performance.
*   **Critically evaluate** the functional prototype against design criteria, user stories, and potential enterprising opportunities or future impacts.
*   **Deliver a multimodal presentation** to communicate the design process, the efficacy of the autonomous solution, and an evaluation of the system’s impact.
